relevance_note: Single case report of a man with ATS 'carrying the homozygous c.1334delG (p.Gly445-Glufs*40) SLC2A10 pathogenic variant'; the Discussion adds three previously published ATS patients with individual-level stroke features.
method_note: Read by hand; no table in the paper; all rows written by a short script from quotes copied from the Markdown and checked verbatim. Scope: the index patient ('patient', rule 5) plus three previously published ATS patients from the Discussion who each have an individual-level feature: two from 'Beyens et Al. ... [1]' (juvenile stroke with intraparenchymal hemorrhage; juvenile stroke with left hemiparesis), labelled 'ref [1] patient' and 'ref [1] patient 2', and the 14-year-old female from 'Cartwright et Al. ... [5]' ('ref [5] patient'). Citation inconsistency: the text attributes the review to 'Beyens et Al.' with reference [1], but reference [1] in the list is Coucke 2006 and Beyens 2018 is reference [2]; source_reference_in_review keeps the text's '[1]'. Prior report: the index patient's variant sentence cites [1, 7] and his aortic surgery cites [7, 8], suggesting earlier publication, but the paper never states that this patient was described before, so cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null and prior_report_citation not reported. n_patients_reported left null: the paper states no number. Contradictions: the Abstract says 'diagnosed with ATS since childhood' while the Case presentation says 'since adolescence' (recorded 'since adolescence'). Doppler in childhood/adolescence showed 'extreme narrowing and tortuosity of the arteries', while MRA and angio-CT at 33 years showed no (hemodynamically significant) stenosis; both feature rows emitted and the checklist item 'stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches' set to not reported. The episodes were diagnosed as TIA with no acute ischemic lesions on MRI, yet the Discussion speaks of 'an embolic genesis of the stroke'; checklist 'stroke or ischemic organ infarction' left not reported for the index patient. Aortic tortuosity left not reported: the angio-CT of 'the thoracic and abdominal aorta' reports 'tortuosity of thoracic and abdominal vessel' and childhood findings concern 'the main arteries', neither naming the aorta itself; tortuosity of other arteries (intracranial, supra-aortic trunks) is observed. Aortic sinus dilation (48 mm) mapped to the checklist item 'aortic root aneurysm' as observed. Dyspnea in childhood mapped to 'respiratory distress or insufficiency' as observed. Absence of dissection and aneurysm was stated only for intracranial and supra-aortic vessels, so the broader checklist item 'arterial dissection' stays not reported. Normal blood pressure recorded as systemic hypertension excluded (D-27). Normal laboratory panels and EEG are recorded as the paper groups them, excluding nothing more specific. Age at onset of ATS not stated (cardiac arrest at delivery recorded as a feature with onset, not as disease onset). Age at last evaluation is the stated age 33; follow-up continued 3 months later. Variant type not stated by the authors for this variant (only 'loss-of-function mutations' for ATS in general); inheritance and parental testing not reported despite consanguinity.
